title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Promoting the Positive Role of Litigation Mediation in Building a Socialist Harmonious Society
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Giving Full Play to the Positive Role of Litigation Mediation in Building a Socialist Harmonious Society"

Fa Fa [2007] No. 9

To: All High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The "Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Giving Full Play to the Positive Role of Litigation Mediation in Building a Socialist Harmonious Society" are hereby issued to you. All courts shall implement them in accordance with actual work circumstances.

March 1, 2007

Supreme People's Court

Several Opinions on Further Giving Full Play to the Positive Role of Litigation Mediation in Building a Socialist Harmonious Society

Proceeding from the overall situation of building a moderately prosperous society in all respects and accelerating socialist modernization, the Sixth Plenary Session of the Sixteenth Central Committee of the Communist Party of China made the major strategic decision to build a socialist harmonious society. The People's Courts are not only a force for building a harmonious society, but also a force for safeguarding it, and bear a significant historical responsibility in the process of building a harmonious society. In order to better adapt to the requirements of the new situation and new tasks, and to fully perform the functions of the People's Courts in resolving conflicts, settling disputes, ensuring economic development, and promoting social harmony, the following opinions are hereby put forward regarding further strengthening litigation mediation work in the People's Courts.

I. Unify Thinking, Enhance Awareness, and Deeply Understand the Great Significance of Litigation Mediation in Building a Harmonious Society

1. Currently, China is in an important period of strategic opportunities and a "golden development period," facing unprecedented opportunities as well as unprecedented challenges. Although China's economy is developing steadily and rapidly, people's living standards have significantly improved, and society is generally harmonious and stable, factors affecting harmony and stability still exist in large numbers. Properly responding to various social conflicts and disputes, coordinating the interests of all parties, effectively平息 disputes, and vigorously promoting social harmony and stability are the overall tasks of the Party and the state. As the state's judicial organs, the People's Courts must unswervingly serve and obey this overall national task and central mission, attach great importance to and fully utilize litigation mediation, an important method for correctly handling social conflicts and an effective means of building a harmonious society, maximize factors of harmony, minimize factors of disharmony, and undertake the major historical mission and political responsibility of promoting and developing a harmonious society.

2. Litigation mediation is an important component of China's litigation system, an important way for the People's Courts to exercise their adjudicative power, and an important part of harmonious justice. It is a dispute resolution method rooted in China's historical and cultural traditions and proven effective through long-term judicial practice. It not only conforms to the values and litigation consciousness of the current public but also embodies the Chinese nation's ideal of pursuing harmony in natural and social order. In recent years, the adjudicative work of the People's Courts has achieved significant development, accumulated valuable experience, and established the guiding principle for civil adjudication of "mediate where possible, adjudicate where appropriate, combine mediation with adjudication, and close the case to settle the dispute." People's Courts at all levels should take "closing the case to settle the dispute" as the goal of adjudicative work, correctly understand the status and role of litigation mediation in the People's Courts' adjudicative work, and vigorously promote litigation mediation work.

3. Give full play to the initiative and enthusiasm of litigation mediation work in People's Courts at all levels, give full play to the wisdom and talent of judges, and carry out litigation mediation work creatively. People's Courts at all levels shall, in accordance with the law and judicial interpretations, and in line with the requirement of "impartial justice, wholehearted service to the people," closely combine local actual conditions, actively explore innovation in litigation mediation mechanisms, improve litigation mediation systems, innovate mediation methods, enhance mediation skills, and comprehensively promote the development of litigation mediation work.

II. Strengthen Mediation, Respect Laws, and Strive to Achieve the Goal of "Closing the Case to Settle the Dispute"

4. Civil adjudicative work should aim at "settling disputes, making clear who wins and who loses, and closing the case to settle the dispute," ensuring the organic unity of legal effect and social effect. People's Courts at all levels must correctly handle the relationship between mediation and adjudication. While further strengthening litigation mediation efforts, increasing the number of cases settled by mediation, and striving to increase the proportion of cases settled by mediation, they should also avoid the tendency of one-sided pursuit of mediation rates. For cases with the possibility of mediation, conditions should be created as far as possible to conduct mediation. For cases that are not suitable for mediation or for which a mediation agreement cannot be reached through efforts, a judgment should be made promptly.

5. For civil cases suitable for settlement by mediation, the People's Courts shall mediate, and shall focus on mediating the following types of cases: cases involving group interests requiring coordination with the government and relevant departments; multi-party joint actions and class actions with a large number of parties; cases with complex facts where the parties are severely emotionally opposed and neither side has a clear evidentiary advantage; cases where relevant laws and regulations have no provisions or unclear provisions, making application of law somewhat difficult; cases of high sensitivity and great social concern; and cases on review of petitions and retrial cases.

6. For criminal cases with附带 civil actions, the People's Courts shall strengthen mediation efforts in accordance with the relevant provisions of civil mediation. For administrative litigation cases, criminal private prosecution cases, and other minor criminal cases, the People's Courts may, based on the actual circumstances of the case, attempt to promote reconciliation between the parties by reference to the principles and procedures of civil mediation. Through the practice of reconciliation in administrative litigation cases, criminal private prosecution cases, and other minor criminal cases, the People's Courts shall continuously explore various case-closing methods conducive to building a harmonious society, continuously innovate methods of litigation reconciliation, promptly summarize experience, and continuously improve the working mechanisms for reconciliation in administrative litigation cases, criminal private prosecution cases, and other minor criminal cases.

7. In litigation mediation, the People's Courts shall take active measures to fully ensure that the parties can truly express their will and exercise their right of disposition in accordance with the law. Ensure that the parties genuinely and voluntarily accept mediation, achieve mutual understanding and mutual accommodation, thoroughly resolve conflicts and eliminate disputes, and achieve the closure of the case to settle the dispute.

8. In litigation mediation, attention should be paid to the propriety, simplicity, and operability of the mediation procedure, avoiding arbitrariness in mediation. The procedures and methods of litigation mediation shall comply with the law and judicial interpretations. The People's Courts shall earnestly fulfill their duties of examining and confirming mediation agreements and reconciliation agreements, ensuring that the agreements do not harm the interests of the state, the public interest, or the lawful rights and interests of others, do not contain content that violates mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and do not contravene good customs and public morality.

III. Innovate Mechanisms, Improve Systems, and Give Full Play to the Role of Litigation Mediation in Resolving Conflicts and Disputes

9. If a mediation agreement reached through mediation by the People's Mediation Committee or other relevant social organizations is not performed by one party, and the other party files a lawsuit with the People's Court requesting performance of the mediation agreement, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Cases Involving People's Mediation Agreements."

10. The People's Courts shall further improve the mediation system at the case-filing stage. After a case is filed and with the consent of the parties, the People's Court may conduct mediation at the case-filing stage. For cases with complex facts where the parties do not consent to mediation, or for cases where the parties cannot be located, they shall be promptly transferred to the trial division for trial. Mediation at the case-filing stage shall adhere to the principles of efficiency and swiftness, avoiding the accumulation of cases at the case-filing stage. For first-instance cases applying summary procedure, the mediation period at the case-filing stage shall generally not exceed 10 days after case filing; for first-instance cases applying ordinary procedure, the mediation period at the case-filing stage shall generally not exceed 20 days. For second-instance cases, case-filing mediation shall generally not be conducted, or a more reasonable mediation period shall be stipulated for second-instance cases.

11. The People's Courts may, in accordance with the law and judicial interpretations, establish and improve working mechanisms for introducing social forces to conduct mediation. The People's Courts may guide the parties to choose mediation by People's Mediation Committees, grass-roots self-governing mass organizations, trade unions, women's federations, and other relevant organizations that are conducive to case mediation, other than the judge handling the case, and may also invite individuals such as People's Congress deputies, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, and lawyers to conduct mediation. With the consent of the parties, judicial assistants and other trial support personnel assigned by the People's Court may also conduct mediation in the case. For difficult, complex, and significantly influential cases, the chief judge of the division or the president of the People's Court may preside over mediation.

12. The People's Courts shall improve mediation norms, perfect mediation procedures, and focus on enhancing the affinity, transparency, and efficiency of mediation work, facilitating the parties' participation in mediation. Based on the actual circumstances of the case, they shall flexibly choose mediation methods and approaches, creating relaxed conditions and atmosphere for the parties to freely negotiate and make mutual concessions. When the People's Court mediates a case, if the parties request open mediation, the People's Court shall permit it; the judge handling the case and the relevant organizations and other individuals participating in mediation shall strictly keep mediation information confidential; if the parties request that the content of the mediation agreement not be disclosed, the People's Court shall permit it.

13. If the parties are willing to conduct mediation but the trial period is about to expire, the parties may negotiate to determine a period for continuing mediation. After examination and approval by the People's Court, the judge handling the case shall record it in the case file. If there is a possibility of reaching a mediation agreement and the parties cannot agree on a period for continuing mediation, with the approval of the president of the court, the mediation period may be reasonably extended.

14. After the parties reach a reconciliation agreement or mediation agreement and apply to the People's Court for the issuance of a mediation statement, the People's Court shall examine the mediation agreement or reconciliation agreement in accordance with the law. The examination content includes: whether the agreement violates mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations; whether it harms the interests of the state or the public interest; whether the content of the agreement falls within the scope of the parties' right of disposition; whether the legal relationship in dispute between the parties involves the rights of persons not party to the case; whether there are rights of persons not party to the case in the property designated for transfer; whether the content of the agreement conforms to good customs and public morality; whether the mediation clearly violates the true intention of the parties, etc.

15. If the parties agree that the mediation agreement shall have legal effect upon signature or seal, this shall be stated in the mediation agreement, and the parties shall sign or seal it, and the judge handling the case and the court clerk shall sign it. The mediation statement produced by the People's Court after examination and confirmation of the reconciliation agreement or mediation agreement shall be signed by the judge handling the case and stamped with the seal of the People's Court.

16. For a mediation agreement that has legal effect after being signed or sealed by the parties, the adjudicators, and the court clerk as provided in Article 13 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Civil Mediation Work," if the parties do not apply for the production of a mediation statement, and one party fails to perform the mediation agreement, and the other party applies for compulsory enforcement based on the effective mediation agreement, the People's Court shall accept the application.

If a retrial case reaches a mediation agreement through mediation and it becomes effective after being signed or sealed by the parties, the judge, and the court clerk, and the parties do not apply for the production of a mediation statement, the People's Court shall issue a ruling to terminate the retrial procedure.

17. If the parties agree that a social organization or individual other than the judge handling the case shall preside over the mediation, and a mediation agreement is reached, the social organization or individual that presided over the mediation shall sign or seal the mediation agreement. However, when the People's Court produces a mediation statement based on the mediation agreement, the social organization or individual that presided over the mediation shall not sign or seal it.

18. For civil enforcement cases, if compulsory enforcement according to all contents of the enforcement basis is truly difficult, with the consent of both parties, the People's Court may organize the parties to reach a settlement. If a settlement agreement is reached through settlement, it shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.

19. For cases where the parties file petitions or apply for retrial, during the process of examination for filing or hearing, if both parties agree to mediation, the People's Court may mediate. If consensus is reached, it may be handled as an enforcement settlement, and the review procedure shall be terminated. If the parties reach a settlement agreement on their own, after examination and confirmation by the People's Court, it may be handled as an enforcement settlement.

20. Each High People's Court may, in accordance with the law and judicial interpretations, unify the format of litigation mediation legal documents and produce templates for litigation mediation documents such as the consent form for mediation before the expiry of the defense period, the application for continued mediation, the letter of entrusted mediation, the decision on litigation costs, and the mediation statement. The content of the mediation statement may be simplified, briefly stating the cause of action and the parties' claims, and may omit the facts of the case, the trial process, and the evidence. The format of a mediation statement that becomes effective upon receipt by the parties and a mediation statement that serves as the basis for compulsory enforcement based on a mediation agreement that has already become effective through the parties' signatures or seals shall be distinguished.

21. The People's Courts shall, based on actual circumstances, establish a scientific and reasonable mediation incentive mechanism to enhance judges' enthusiasm and initiative in mediation. The results of mediation work shall be included in the scope of individual performance evaluation. The mediation incentive mechanism should not only reflect affirmation and encouragement of mediation work but also avoid the tendency of one-sided pursuit of mediation rates.

22. To give full play to the positive role of litigation mediation in building a harmonious society, the focus is at the grassroots level, and the key lies in the grassroots. Grassroots People's Courts directly face the public, hear most first-instance cases, and bear the main task of resolving conflicts and disputes and maintaining social stability. Whether the litigation mediation work of grassroots People's Courts is well done directly determines the effect of litigation mediation work nationwide and directly affects the foundation of social stability and harmony. High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts shall attach importance to and increase guidance, support, and assistance for litigation mediation work in grassroots People's Courts, increase support for grassroots People's Courts in personnel, finances, and materials, strive to resolve most conflicts at the grassroots level, solve problems at the grassroots level, and ensure that conflicts are not expanded, intensified, or escalated.

23. The People's Courts shall earnestly study and explore the establishment of a docking mechanism between litigation procedures and extra-litigation dispute resolution mechanisms, adhere to adjudicative work as the center, strengthen guidance to People's Mediation Organizations, vigorously support and legally supervise the mediation work of other organizations, actively promote the establishment and improvement of a diversified social dispute resolution mechanism, and give full play to the role of all sectors of society in alleviating conflicts and resolving disputes.

IV. Strengthen Training, Promote Exchange, and Vigorously Improve Judges' Litigation Mediation Ability

24. People's Courts at all levels shall attach great importance to the construction of judges' litigation mediation ability, making this work a key focus of court team building that is persistently carried out. Training on judges' mediation ability shall be intensified, long-term training plans shall be formulated, and a rotation training system for judges shall be established. High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts shall provide comprehensive support for the training of judges from grassroots People's Courts. When necessary, a higher People's Court may organize training for judges of lower People's Courts. The Supreme People's Court shall annually hold a mediation ability training class for some judges.

25. People's Courts at all levels shall fully recognize that judges' judicial ability is a comprehensive ability, including both the ability to preside over courtroom trials and the ability to mediate cases. To strengthen judges' ability construction, based on the basic requirements of court team building, judges' ability to preside over trials and mediate shall be vigorously improved. Continuously perfect mediation skills, innovate mediation methods, and improve judges' ability to resolve disputes in a harmonious manner.

26. People's Courts at all levels shall strengthen the summarization and exchange of experience in litigation mediation. In recent years, courts nationwide have gained a wealth of valuable experience in innovation of litigation mediation mechanisms, improvement of systems, and reform of mediation methods, and a large number of litigation mediation experts have emerged. Summarization and promotion of these valuable experiences shall be intensified, especially focusing on summarization and exchange of mediation work experience for certain types of difficult and complex cases, to promote the continuous development of litigation mediation work.
